second_pass_methodology: RE-RESEARCH security focus 2026-05-24. Goal: resolve ⚠️ → ✅ or 🔴 by proving (or disproving) the operator's SECURITY INVARIANT: every WhatsApp send path goes through the HR-05 allowlist (lines 73-108), and no path bypasses it. Audited: (1) every caller of sendWhatsAppTemplate, (2) every direct fetch to graph.facebook.com in the entire dashboard-web/src/ tree, (3) the operator-UI test-send route + WhatsappTestButtons, (4) the token-failure notifier path, (5) the Inngest cron worker stack, (6) recent commits since baseline b846ae7. Methodology: `grep -rn 'sendWhatsAppTemplate' dashboard-web/src/` returns exactly 2 callers; `grep -rn 'graph.facebook.com.*messages' dashboard-web/src/` returns exactly 1 POST (whatsapp.ts:131). No other code path constructs the Meta WhatsApp Cloud HTTP request.

indirect_paths_audited.path: /api/operator/notifications/send POST → inngest.send('notifications/whatsapp.send-now') → eventWhatsappSendNow worker → sendDailySummary() → sendWhatsAppTemplate() → allowlist gate
indirect_paths_audited.rationale: The route itself does NOT call sendWhatsAppTemplate directly. It dispatches an Inngest event and returns 202. The worker funnels through sendDailySummary which uses the SAME DB-config recipients and SAME wrapper. No alternate send code path.

Client UI only POSTs to the same route; no client-side allowlist override possible. The trigger enum is validated server-side (route.ts:30) against {'noon','evening','eod'} — no path to inject a recipient.
All three crons call sendDailySummary() which uses DB-config recipients and routes through sendWhatsAppTemplate → allowlist gate.
Hardcoded ALERT_PHONE='+972524809540' → sendWhatsAppTemplate → allowlist gate. Even though the hardcode already matches the contract, it still goes through the allowlist (defense in depth).

normalization_correctness_audit.rationale: Both the allowlist and the recipient are normalized to the SAME canonical form (digits only, no plus, no separators) before the includes() check. Array.includes() uses strict equality, NOT substring match — so a recipient '972524809540' cannot accidentally match an allowlist entry '+1972524809540' (normalizes to '1972524809540' — different string). Edge cases checked: leading '+' (stripped), embedded dashes/parens/spaces (stripped by [^0-9]), country-code-only entry without phone digits (still works — both sides apply the same rule). No normalization-collision bypass possible.

configuration_injection_audit.rationale: grep -rn 'WHATSAPP_RECIPIENT_OVERRIDE' dashboard-web/src/ returns NO matches. The only allowlist-related env var is NOTIFICATION_RECIPIENT_ALLOWLIST itself, which is the ALLOWLIST DEFINITION — it can only RESTRICT the recipient set, never expand a bypass. No code path reads any 'override' or 'bypass' env var to skip the allowlist check. Conclusion: env-var injection cannot bypass the allowlist.

When unset, recipientAllowed() returns {allowed: true} permissively (back-compat shim, whatsapp.ts:96). This is by design and documented in code comments (lines 84-87) and finding SVC-02 from the first review.
security_invariant_status.single_chokepoint: dashboard-web/src/lib/notifications/whatsapp.ts:131 — the only fetch() call to graph.facebook.com/.../messages in the entire dashboard-web/src/ tree. Every send funnels through it.

uncertainty_notes_resolved: Second-pass verdict: ✅ Verified. The HR-05 allowlist is the single chokepoint for ALL WhatsApp delivery. Every caller of sendWhatsAppTemplate (sendDailySummary.ts:76, tokenFailures.ts:227) funnels through the allowlist gate at whatsapp.ts:124-130 before the fetch at line 131. There is exactly ONE POST to graph.facebook.com/.../messages in the entire dashboard-web/src/ tree (whatsapp.ts:131). The /api/operator/notifications/send route dispatches an Inngest event (no direct send), and the event handler routes through sendDailySummary. Normalization is symmetric (allowlist line 101 + recipient line 119 use the same regex), and the match is strict-equality via Array.includes() — no substring or normalization-collision bypass. No WHATSAPP_RECIPIENT_OVERRIDE env var exists. CAVEAT: the allowlist is permissive when NOTIFICATION_RECIPIENT_ALLOWLIST is unset (back-compat); operator MUST set this env var on Vercel for the runtime boundary to enforce — this is a deployment-config requirement, already documented in code comments and SVC-02. Verdict moves from ⚠️ to ✅ because the code-level boundary is provably airtight; the deployment-config caveat is correctly documented and is not a bug per se.
